court: Court of Appeals for the First Circuit

issues.label: Jurisdiction over first petition after reconsideration
issues.why: The first petition (No. 25-1340) challenged an order superseded by the granted reconsideration, raising mootness and jurisdictional questions.

issues.label: Effect of granting reconsideration on prior order
issues.why: The court must determine whether the granted reconsideration replaced or merely supplemented the March order for review purposes.

issues.label: Timeliness of petitions for review
issues.why: Whether each petition was filed within the statutory 30-day window relative to the operative final BIA order.

issues.label: Scope of consolidated review
issues.why: The court must decide which BIA rulings and reasoning are properly before it in the consolidated petitions.

issues.label: Standard of review applied
issues.why: Factual findings reviewed for substantial evidence and legal conclusions de novo shape the entire analysis.

issues.label: Exhaustion of administrative remedies
issues.why: Only issues raised before the BIA are generally reviewable, affecting which arguments the court can consider.

issues.label: Definition of particular social group 'family'
issues.why: Whether family constitutes a cognizable particular social group and its correct delineation must be assessed.

issues.label: Nexus to protected ground
issues.why: The court must confirm past harm was 'on account of' family, not merely private violence.

issues.label: Sufficiency of past persecution finding
issues.why: Whether the childhood abuse from father, age mates, and Mungiki members legally rises to persecution.

issues.label: Rebuttal via changed country conditions
issues.why: Whether substantial evidence supports that Kenyan police efforts against Mungiki rebut the presumption.

issues.label: Rebuttal via applicant's changed age
issues.why: Whether reaching adulthood and escaping father's control adequately rebuts future persecution presumption.

issues.label: Individualized rebuttal analysis required
issues.why: DHS bears the burden and must show changed conditions negate this applicant's specific fear.

issues.label: Consideration of non-father sources of harm
issues.why: The BIA initially overlooked harm from age mates and Mungiki members, requiring reassessment of the rebuttal.

issues.label: Whether age alone eliminates Mungiki threat
issues.why: The record describes Mungiki as broader than paternal control, undermining the 'no longer a child' rationale.

issues.label: Government unwilling/unable to protect
issues.why: Persecution by non-state actors requires assessing whether Kenya can control the Mungiki.

issues.label: Humanitarian asylum severity standard
issues.why: Whether the past harm was severe enough for compelling-reasons humanitarian asylum under 8 C.F.R. 1208.13(b)(1)(iii)(A).

issues.label: Humanitarian asylum other-serious-harm prong
issues.why: Whether a reasonable possibility of other serious harm on return was properly evaluated.

issues.label: Discretionary denial of asylum
issues.why: Whether the IJ's discretionary denial based on U.S. law-enforcement encounters was proper and supported.

issues.label: Withholding of removal analysis
issues.why: Whether denial can rest solely on the failed asylum claim given differing burdens and standards.

issues.label: Withholding future-harm government finding
issues.why: The IJ's cryptic 'government unwilling and unable' finding must be adequately explained and supported.

issues.label: CAT torture likelihood determination
issues.why: Whether Muchiri showed he is more likely than not to be tortured with official acquiescence.

issues.label: Adequacy of BIA's reasoning
issues.why: Whether the BIA sufficiently explained its conclusions, especially after correcting its factual error, to permit review.

issues.label: Whether remand is required
issues.why: If the BIA's rationale is flawed or incomplete, the court must decide between reversal and remand under Ventura.

issues.label: Credibility finding's binding effect
issues.why: The IJ found Muchiri credible, so his testimony must be accepted in evaluating all claims.

issues.label: Harm as child versus persecution timing
issues.why: Whether the BIA properly discounted incidents because they occurred during childhood.
